steps.tx: A **vitamin B12 deficiency** results from impaired intake, absorption, or transport of cobalamin, an organometallic micronutrient synthesized exclusively by microorganisms. Humans depend on dietary animal products such as meat, dairy, and eggs. Because the liver stores two to five milligrams of cobalamin and daily physiological turnover is only one to two micrograms, dietary deficiency takes three to five years of strict veganism to manifest.
steps.say: Vitamin B12, or cobalamin, is synthesized only by bacteria, so humans must obtain it from meat, dairy, and eggs. The human liver holds a massive reserve of two to five milligrams against a tiny daily requirement of one to two micrograms. That is why it takes three to five years of strict veganism to deplete body stores.

vis.caption: Gastric intrinsic factor pathway and spinal cord demyelination in vitamin B12 deficiency.

steps.tx: Physiological absorption requires complex **gastric intrinsic factor** transport. In the acidic stomach, pepsin releases dietary cobalamin to bind salivary haptocorrin. In the duodenum, pancreatic proteases degrade haptocorrin, allowing B12 to bind intrinsic factor, a glycoprotein secreted by gastric parietal cells. The B12-intrinsic factor complex travels to the terminal ileum, binding to specialized cubam surface receptors for calcium-dependent endocytosis.
steps.say: Absorption is a relay race. In the stomach, B12 binds salivary haptocorrin. In the duodenum, pancreatic enzymes strip haptocorrin away, handing B12 over to intrinsic factor secreted by gastric parietal cells. This B12-intrinsic factor complex travels down to the terminal ileum, where it binds cubam receptors for absorption.

vis.title: Gastrointestinal Absorption Milestones
rows: Acid and pepsin liberate B12; parietal cells secrete IF
Atrophic gastritis, gastrectomy, proton pump inhibitors
Crohn disease, ileal resection, tapeworm (D. latum)

steps.tx: The most common etiology of severe deficiency is **pernicious anaemia**, an autoimmune disorder characterized by immune destruction of gastric parietal cells and chronic atrophic gastritis. Circulating autoantibodies target gastric parietal cells (anti-parietal cell antibodies, ninety percent sensitive) and intrinsic factor (anti-IF antibodies, ninety-five percent specific). Achlorhydria and elevated serum gastrin levels develop, with an increased risk of gastric adenocarcinoma.
steps.say: Pernicious anaemia is the leading cause of severe B12 deficiency. Autoimmune T cells destroy gastric parietal cells, causing atrophic gastritis and loss of intrinsic factor. Anti-parietal cell antibodies are ninety percent sensitive, while anti-intrinsic factor antibodies are ninety-five percent specific. The chronic gastritis also carries an elevated lifetime risk of gastric cancer.

right.title: Anti-Intrinsic Factor Antibodies
points: Block B12 binding or ileal cubam receptor
Present in 50 to 70% of pernicious anaemia

steps.tx: Cobalamin serves as an essential cofactor for two vital intracellular enzymes: methionine synthase and **methylmalonyl-CoA mutase**. Methionine synthase utilizes methyl-cobalamin to convert homocysteine into methionine; its deficiency traps folate as N5-methyl-THF (the folate trap). Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase uses adenosyl-cobalamin to isomerize methylmalonyl-CoA into succinyl-CoA. In B12 deficiency, methylmalonic acid and homocysteine both accumulate in serum, whereas folate deficiency elevates homocysteine alone.
steps.say: B12 runs two vital enzymes. Methionine synthase turns homocysteine into methionine. Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase turns methylmalonyl-CoA into succinyl-CoA. In B12 deficiency, both homocysteine and methylmalonic acid build up in blood. In folate deficiency, only homocysteine is elevated while methylmalonic acid remains completely normal, cleanly separating the two.

vis.title: Biochemical Differentiation: B12 versus Folate
rows: Specific marker of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase failure
Best indicator of long-term tissue folate stores

steps.tx: Unlike folate deficiency, cobalamin depletion inflicts irreversible neurological injury presenting as **subacute combined degeneration** of the spinal cord. Defective methylation impairs myelin sheath maintenance, causing symmetrical demyelination of the posterior dorsal columns (loss of vibration and position sense with sensory ataxia) and lateral corticospinal tracts (spastic paraparesis). Administering folic acid alone without B12 corrects the anaemia but tragically accelerates irreversible paraplegia.
steps.say: B12 deficiency destroys myelin, causing subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord. Demyelination strikes the posterior columns, wiping out vibration and proprioception, and the lateral corticospinal tracts, causing spastic leg weakness. Never treat megaloblastic anaemia with folate alone without ruling out B12 deficiency, because folate cures the anaemia while letting spinal cord damage march to irreversible paralysis.

left.title: Subacute Combined Degeneration
points: Posterior column: loss of position and vibration
Lateral corticospinal: spastic paraparesis and Babinski

right.title: Folate Trap Pitfall
points: Always measure B12 before administering high-dose folate

quiz.q: Which metabolic assay cleanly differentiates vitamin B12 deficiency from folate deficiency?
options: Serum methylmalonic acid (elevated in B12 deficiency, normal in folate deficiency)
Serum total homocysteine (elevated in B12 deficiency, absent in folate deficiency)
Red blood cell mean corpuscular volume (elevated only in B12 deficiency)
Serum lactate dehydrogenase (elevated only in folate deficiency)
quiz.explain: Serum methylmalonic acid is elevated in B12 deficiency due to methylmalonyl-CoA mutase failure, but remains completely normal in folate deficiency, whereas homocysteine is elevated in both.

quiz.q: Why is administering high-dose folic acid alone contraindicated in an undiagnosed megaloblastic anaemia?
options: It corrects the haematological anaemia while allowing neurological demyelination to worsen irreversibly
It precipitates acute fatal intravascular hemolysis within 24 hours
It induces acute hyperkalemia and cardiac conduction block
It accelerates conversion of latent leukaemia into acute blast crisis
quiz.explain: Folate overcomes the thymidylate synthase block to resolve the macrocytic anaemia, but fails to prevent or reverse the demyelinating spinal cord damage of subacute combined degeneration.
